title: Why Recycling Plants Break Glass on Purpose #shorts
summary: At a material recovery facility a glass breaker shatters glass so it falls through a screen, and a cyclone lifts the lighter paper and plastic off it (City of Calgary). About 31% of US glass containers were recycled in 2018 (US EPA).
sources: How a material recovery facility sorts a blue cart: trucks unload, workers pre-sort plastic bags and hazardous items by hand, disc screens lift cardboard and flat paper, a glass breaker shatters glass so it falls through a screen and a cyclone lifts lighter paper and plastic off it, optical sorters with air jets, a magnet picks up tin cans, an eddy current 'acts like a magnet in reverse' and repels foil, cans and pie plates onto another belt, sorted material is baled and sold; '90% automated sorting by machines', 'the other 10% is handled manually'; 'garbage bags are never opened during the sorting process'; destinations: plastics to Canada, metal cans and foil to Eastern Canada, cardboard to Canada and the US, paper to Eastern Canada, the US, India, Malaysia and Taiwan, glass to Western Canada (City of Calgary, How the recycling facility works): https://www.calgary.ca/uep/wrs/recycling-information/residential-services/blue-cart-recycling/how-recycling-works.html

Corrugated boxes recycled at 96.5% in 2018; aluminum beverage cans 50.4% (670,000 tons); glass containers 31.3% (3.1 million tons); PET bottles and jars 29.1%; plastic containers and packaging 13.6% (US EPA, Containers and Packaging: Product-Specific Data, 2018 data): https://www.epa.gov/facts-and-figures-about-materials-waste-and-recycling/containers-and-packaging-product-specific

scenes.narration: Recycling plants break your glass on purpose.
A glass breaker shatters it, so the pieces drop through a screen.
Then a cyclone sucks up the lighter paper and plastic. The glass is too heavy, so it stays.
About {31%|thirty-one percent} of US glass containers got recycled in {2018|twenty eighteen}.
So glass gets sorted by being smashed first. In other words...
